chapterTitle: Chapter 3: Synaptic Memoriam of a steel fossil shell
editorText:
<$Proj_H::1><!$Proj_H::1>

A strange little Mechanoid being, not dissimilar from John’s newfound body in appearance, placed his hand on the sides of the cavern. “Little guy looks like me..” John thought to himself looking over at Tau as his rifle sites reticle readjusted to capture the figure sheltered by a wall of mist and steam billowing outward into the tunnel as the cold atmosphere bathed the battery cells nested beneath a large EMP cannon.

“Seems friendly enough” Shai looked back at Tex who was still coming too with a smirk. Tex thought for a moment it to be a straw. It wasn’t a man, but it had a heartbeat. Completely  “We’re protectant.. said Tau, but.. bastards?” She questioned the integrity of the little machine mans analysis and to whom it was directed, thinking it awfully suspicious. “Marcellus” John thought quietly to himself. Tau was confused. She was expecting to be torn apart by a barrage of fire only to find ths friendly little machine man. “It was aiming at you ya daft bastard, that means your it’s enemy and my enemies foe is my friend..”  “Seems more human than machine.”, john through to himself”. “your a , your a hybrid too!”. Said John walking over now with a friendly body language his rifle at his side. Johns voice softened like he had met a long lost friend at a tech conference. “Yep, tasked by the Dr to maintain this facility”. What the hell are you doing so close to the surface? We thought this place was uninhabited. only investigated because we picked up on the break in your sound barrier”.:Tau was puzzled.. “Aaah yes, I was up here fixing the dam transformer thermal cell. The tectonic shifts in this region can be troublesome to all this hardware. We are still perfecting the Nano bots..” The little machine man knelt down pulling a cylinder from his hip. It ejected from a well formed storage capsule intricately and conveniently blended into the stream line of his frame where intestines would normally be on a human. “That drone picked up on your Barrier break as an impulse anomaly when you entered into our little sanctuary and broke the sound/light barrier”

Tau stood up brushing the dirt from her suits targeting reticle. “That explains why it still showed up even after we were behind the curtain, it detects large breaks in the curtain, and drew a sound profile of our suits from the static crackles,

“What do we call you?” said Tau in a motherly tone. “Our Ally?” Said John, leaning his back into the tunnel wall as he caught his composure, his rifle slouching at his side.

The little machine man rested the lid of the cylinder on the grate below him, gently nursing a small straggling mass from behind a chrome trail of liquid thick substance within an oil based medium. “We are still working through the transition medium to increase repair times. But these guys will shift the transformer plates in time to correct the bump in our hard light emitter by noon” The being tightened the cap resealing the remaining nanobots inside it, then reinserted it into it’s holder in his waist. “” He said seeming awfully pleased with himself. “To a spiritual awakening? are these mushrooms going to teleport us to another dimension” Tex seemed amused with his little joke as he squished some of the lichen and moss between his fingers, flicking it to the ground.

Spending months on end in an airtight can in space had invoked a child-like curiosity in the man. His visor retracted as he indulged his senses. “Some might call it another dimension, my gentle giant!” said Tbone leaning up against the cavern wall, a mischievous smile was stretched across his face. “Cap” Whispered Tau. “I’m picking up allot of electrical activity”. Taus visor was locked shut still as she observed a plethora of signal activity. While Tex found it hard to contain impulsive thoughts, she had remained reserved still, unsure with their new acquaintance. “It’s fine” Said Walker, unbothered by the humm which began to reverberate through the cavern. The rear of the cavern wall glitched for a moment, John, Tau Shai and Tex all stepped back harrowed for a moment, squinting, gleaning whether what they had just seen was real. They’d seen small Hard mesh cloaks before but something of this scale seemed unusual, new, unexpected. A sudden beeping sound chimed 5 times. Then a deep electronic voice gauged their ears in a horrid cryptic language they had never heard before. The sound entered the room like a bus horn easing down with electronic inflections, whips and clack's as the frequencies twisted and turned, it was almost painful to the others but John seemed unphased.

“What the fuck was that” Tex raised his rifle straight at Tbone’s head his finger on the trigger ready to paint the walls with his brains or whatever the fuck was inside he thought to himself. John croaked gently in a dissuasive tone, “Tex! lower your weapon”, accompanied by a restraining wave at his side. The tension in the air receded but not fully. Tex’s rifle muzzle dipped to the ground as he let out a deep sigh in a mix of relief, then disbelief. He gasped in awe wide eyed as the entirety of the cavern's rear wall dissolved into nothingness.

“Hard Light Mesh Technology, but.. of this scale!?” Tau spoke with admiration as the young Engineer stepped forward with inquisitiveness Tex looked on at her. Her rifle now mag-locked across her back, Tex shrugged his shoulders then holstered his rifle in its place. An electronic humm filled the cavern's belly with an otherworldly presence emitting from towering blast doors which spanned the entirety of the cavern rear.

“Have we inhaled some funky mushroom spores?” Tex wondered aloud, his voice tinged with wonder and confusion. Tbone, arms folded in contemplation, posed a question that hung in the air like a riddle awaiting unraveling. “How do you think those mushrooms got there?” he explained, his gaze filled with pride spanned the belly of the cave like a fathers eyes resting on the womb containing his child. "Artificial light breathes life into this abyss, sustaining us in secrecy.”

Tbone had his arms crossed waiting for an answer from Tex, but more he seemed disappointed he had so swiftly raised his rifle straight at his head. He didn’t think he would pull the trigger, but he could sense the distrust in the man. He didn’t blame him either. His whole squad had just been crossed by their own faction, everything they knew. “So much remains hidden from all of you, you’ve all been fooled” Tbone thought to himself, then unfolded his arms walking over to the towering blast doors. The Doors looked ancient. Their scale projected a sense of Alien Majesty, as they hummed like an ethereal soul. Tau was shaken by how someone or something could have amassed the material to procure such a feat of engineering so deep underneath the mountains, little own withstand the active shifts in the tectonic plates and hold it’s structural integrity. “How on earth did this all get here?” Tbone unfolded his hand resting it on a small recessed face at the edge of the blast doors frame. “This is just the tip of the iceberg my friends” Tebo smiled at Tau, then the same harrowing sound from before let out, but this time less intense than the first.

The colossal blast doors shuddered in the wake of the sound as though they had been awoken. They slowly began to retract inch by inch they disappeared into the stoney mass of the cavern walls. As they opened an emptiness of thick mist bellowed out in waves, engulfing them up to their knees pushing past them to settle along the top of the water runs at the foot of the green room mother tree.

A fine sand like dust trickled down from the giant doors weathered crevasses gently caressing the foundation at it’s base, as though to bestow those before her with the majesty of her scale and meaning. The cave seemed to rattle and shake, yet in reality it remained still, a deception cast over the mind due to the sheer scale of the towering doors as they carried the room as they moved making it hard to determine what was actually moving.

“Why all the theatrics? That sound!” said Tex, “We figured any scavengers might be deterred by something they couldn’t understand should they stray too far. Nonetheless, most of them, the curious few that slipped through only made it to the green room, I think they thought it was cursed or something because they never stayed too long within its hold. In total over the last half century only 4 have made it to the green room”. As the last words slipped from the little machine man’s mouth the blast doors let out a heavy clap as they finished their retreat into the walls, then everything was silent. The others retracted their visors looking out gleaning into the darkness with questions. A cold chill blew in through the massive opening kissing Tex and the others on the face. The force of the wind whispered to the scale of the open space before them.

John was the first to step forward, a slight metallic thud after each step but with minimal echo. The steel beneath him was thick and he could feel it, like a foundation to support the towers of an empire. With each step his eyes toyed with intricate patterns interweaving along the structure's surface, they were unlike anything he had seen before, a cryptic lingual dance of an unknown civilisation. They spanned the entirety of the structure, beckoning him forward, further to a pronounced edge where the patterns cut in then down to the depths. John’s rifle rested quietly in it’s maglock cradle as the captain let the suit carry him carelessly forward. John Stood firmly now at the edge.The tension in his shoulders eased off as they as his gaze lay rest over an industrious underground womb. John’s pupils dilated in a euphoric state gleaning deeper into the depths of something beyond the realms of the human mind.

John's part-sentient eyes gifted him with a true understanding of the depths and scale of the realm before him. As his eyes crept down the ledge from beneath his armour clad toes, the ledge beneath him began to violently glow. Thermal ducts sprawled out - a vast network of energy, violently glew, transitioning from dark blues to amber clouds as electrons swirled in intricate turbulence dancing with one another interlocked in a perpetuating dance amidst a web of steel, stone, ice, and flora.

Tau was the next to make it to the ledge, her rifle slightly raised in caution she stood to the left of John, trailing behind her Shai and Tex together looking out almost symmetrically together in opposite sectors, the little machine man wandered carefree behind the group, his hands and fingers interlocked behind his back, resting behind his metallic hips. He allowed the silence to stagnate, curious to see how his new-found friends would perceive his birthplace.

“How long have you been down here?” Tau couldn’t hold her thoughts any longer, curiosity cutting through the silence like a Niten Ichiryu blades edge. “What do you mean?” Said the little robotic man. He stopped for a moment pondering the question “Well since the Dr brought me into this place, what I remember of it anyway. He said I was a mechanic before he repurposed me here, and well I’ve been looking after Genesis ever since”, “Two heavens as one” Tau looked at Tebo, all was quiet as he made eye contact with her. “Yes, my second heaven”. Shai stepped forward to the ledge with the others, looking out over a utopia teeming with organic life.

Suspended networks of interwoven thermal ducts all tied into a larger cylindrical tower at the center of the cavern. The cylinder glew a dim blue in John’s eyes as the ducts pulsed bringing it to life. Tau could not see the thermal duct taps into the earth's crust like John, but the Engineer inside her appreciated the design before her.

“John.. Do you mind if I..”,  “Tap in?” John finished Tao’s sentence like he could feel her curiosity creeping up on him. “Kitten bridge my optics to Taus viewport please” .Tau was silently appreciating the beauty of the gardens as they hung like a window, veering deep into the past, she felt like a child walking through the gardens of Babylon. Streams of quartz clear water trickled down overgrown structures, her mind riding on a journey to the depths of another realm. Thickets of vines writhed around massive hydraulic legs, entangling themselves in a fumbling dance to grip to any impurities that presented a hold on the seamlessly immaculate towering steel structures. Finally they found purchase, digging into and around the milder steel wings assisting them as they held the rubble from crushing below. Their tendrils seemed to reach down ever searching, as they looked back over their new companions' wandering heads. Shai's neck worked up a mild whiplash as she tracked their movements with awe."

As the Little Machine Man Tbone stepped forward he opened his arms out wide softly pronouncing. “I present to you.. Genesis”.. The moment the name emitted from the little machine it echoed through what felt like an eternity, Taus' vision blew up with life and heat signatures dancing underneath the structures foundations, every pillars roots shooting down, glowing like a giver of life, feeding a chasm of systems both natural and artificial the warmth and energy needed like a tree from the depths. “Now you see what I see huh” Tau looked into John's eyes and smiled, with a hint of intimacy, although John didn’t pick up on it. He was gone, his gaze lost, gleaning deeper into the center of the cavernous underground superstructure in wonder of what lay within its embracing depths.

Tex stumbled back in astonishment “Fuuck me, You fuckers have been busy!”Tex muttered, his concern evident as he cautiously approached the ledge behind the group.

Overhead his eyes bounced over the array of giant steel wings that spanned across from either side of the cavern. A display of strength and superior ingenuity on a scale none of them had seen implemented in their time. The wings were Suspended from towering hydraulic shafts that dug down into solid steel boots protruding out across the floor of the bunker. “I've never seen underground mining technology to this scale” Tex was busy contemplating how it all pieced together, how a full scale operational underground ship yard had been pieced together with the remnants of what seemed like mobile underground mining props.

“Everything serves its purpose down here.. and when it meets the end of it’s purpose.. it is repurposed” Tbone unfolded his hands presenting the cascading arches before his robotic palms.. “We are fortunate the Protectant selected such a resource rich location to base the workerbot project, or as the Dr re-termed it.. Project Serva Vitae”. as the Projects name left the little machine man’s lips the ground beneath John and his teams began to vibrate. They felt their legs fall beneath stumbled to recorrect their balance. A small half hexagon they had all been standing within on the ledge amidst seclusive patterns emerged a deeper ridge that grew higher. The ledge they once stood upon began to rise up beyond their chests. By now John’s team had been overcome by the experience and ambience of it all, they were hooked now. the environment was overtaking them, And they let it happen. They allowed themselves to be taken by the grasp of where the little machine Man was taking them.

Solid ridges of an Unknown alloy akin to mild steel glew softly with the kiss of an alien-like insignia. Patterns etched deep like a circuit of veins pumping life into the facility as they creeped down along the now towering walls which had risen increasing faster above them as they gained velocity downwards. They had descended deeper towards the base of the first towering shafts that the immense scale of the prop boots at the base of the shaft spoke of a scale Tex questioned even with his experience the practicality and ridiculous deposits of minerals these props would have been used to extract from the depths. He couldn’t understand how Men would be able to service mining infrastructure so big. It didn’t make sense in his practical mind. “What the Fuck were you mining down here?” he spoke more to himself than anyone. When the platform reached the bottom the shafts hummed ever louder than before. “The  to Oasis”. The little machine man answered Tex like it was obvious.

A subtle glow in the lingering light of the bunker, They seemed to beckon everyone forward along it’s belly between the immense shaft bases that stood firm with feet which now felt like Gaurds watching over them, protecting them, holding the shafts firmly in place. A path a clearing shot past up the center of the towering glowing shafts deeper into the bunkers hold, or it’s release John thought to himself. the facility seemed to humm gently to them calling them in. John more than any of them felt this. Like he was being called home, yet while in a foreign alien place he had never imagined nor seen, this place felt nostalgic. As blue and amber light wisped within the quarts of John’s visor he imagined himself as a child. Only eight years old, opening the door to his fathers laboratory, warm white light from the hallway domestic globes melding with the glow of soft blue digital oscilloscopes and sound spectrometers. The walls reminded him of his fathers solitary study. He was but a firefly drawn to the familiar comfort of a light which he knew to be all too familiar.

“The origins of the Sentient integration ship that now lies in wait for us on the shifting plates of Oasis.”
